URL: https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistani-airstrikes-afghanistan-kill-nine-kabul-says-2026-10-01/
Reuters (Kabul) — published 1 October 2026, 03:23 UTC (04:23 BST)

Pakistani airstrikes on Afghanistan killed 9 people and injured 11 more on Thursday, the Afghan Taliban government said, amid an escalation in fighting between the South Asian neighbours after three months of relative calm.
- The strikes destroyed three houses in Kunar and Helmand provinces, Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid said on X.
- At least nine people were killed, including women and children, he said.
QUOTE (Zabihullah Mujahid, spokesman for Afghanistan's Taliban government): "We condemn this act as an aggression and crime in violation of all accepted principles."
- Reuters could not independently verify the information.
- Allies-turned-foes Pakistan and Afghanistan have increasingly been at odds over militancy, with Islamabad accusing Kabul of harbouring militants who stage cross-border attacks. The Taliban government denies the charge.

AP wire (Abdul Qahar Afghan and Elena Becatoros, 1 Oct 2026 01:13 EDT) — carried by wdtn.com; NOT found on an approved domain in my sweep, so treat the Pakistani side's figures with care:
- Pakistan's Ministry of Information said its strikes were against militant hideouts in two locations and that "initial reports suggest" 22 militants had been killed.
- QUOTE (Pakistan Ministry of Information statement): strikes were "well planned and calibrated" against militant hideouts and camps and "been carried out in Afghanistan with precision and accuracy"; "The threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan... Our action precisely targeted the terrorist hubs"; "Maximum precautions were taken and it was ensured that no collateral damage occurs."
- Pakistan accuses the Taliban of allowing Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to operate from Afghan territory; the TTP is separate from but allied with the Afghan Taliban, who seized power in 2021.
NOTE: Pakistan's own Radio Pakistan (radio.gov.pk, 1 Oct 06:25) names the targets as "Fitna al Khwarij and Fitna al Hindustan" — Pakistani state outlet, NOT approved.
NOTE: Amu TV (not approved) says this is the third round of Pakistani air attacks inside Afghanistan in the past 10 days (21 Sep in Kunar and Paktika; a later round in Kandahar, Paktia and Khost), and that an attack on a police facility in north-west Pakistan last month killed 24 people.
